narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and your credit history. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest driver pushing the decision toward denial. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have accounts in this state, while the majority (59.2%) have no checking account at all. This negative status signaled higher risk to the model.

The 42-month duration you requested was the second most important factor and also increased the likelihood of being seen as a bad risk. Approved loans average only 19 months, so your longer term stood out as substantially above the norm.

Your credit history marked as “critical or other existing credits” worked in the opposite direction. This actually pulled the prediction slightly toward approval. However, its positive influence was not strong enough to overcome the negative effects of your account status and loan length.

Given these results, you should first improve the status of your checking account and consider applying for a shorter-term loan that is closer to the average duration of successfully approved applications. Addressing these two areas gives you the best chance of a different outcome in the future. (218 words)
